```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Survey and administrative data from Bangladesh have the same problems again
and again: mobile numbers typed in ten ways, money written as "1.5 lakh" or
"Tk 25,000/-", Bangla digits, and place names spelled differently in every
source and differently again in the boundary files used for maps. bdscrub
fixes these with eleven functions and reports every change it makes.

```{r}
library(bdscrub)
```

## Mobile numbers

```{r}
x <- c("01712345678", "+880 1712-345678", "8801812345678", "1912345678",
       "0171234567", "01712345678 / 01812345678", NA)
bd_phone(x, warn = FALSE)
bd_phone(x, format = "e164", multiple = "first", warn = FALSE)
bd_phone(x, details = TRUE)
```

A cell with two numbers gives `NA` by default, because choosing one is a
decision; `multiple = "first"` makes that decision explicit.

## Money and numbers

```{r}
inc <- c("Tk 1,25,000", "1.5 lakh", "1 crore 25 lakh", "500/-", "25k",
         "15-20k", "about 5 lakh", "Tk 25,00")
bd_amount(inc, warn = FALSE)
bd_amount(inc, details = TRUE)
bd_number(c("1,25,000", " 34 ", "34 years"), warn = FALSE)
bd_taka(c(125000, 12500000), prefix = "Tk ")
```

Ranges and approximate amounts are not exact amounts, so they are `NA` in the
plain result; `details = TRUE` keeps their lower and upper ends for the
analysis to decide.

## Place names

```{r}
bd_place(c("Chittagong", "jessore district", "Munshigonj", "COX'S BAZAR",
           "Nababganj", "Kishorgnj"))
bd_place(c("Chattogram", "Brahmanbaria"), style = "map")
bd_place(c("Kaliganj", "Kaliganj", "Sadar", "Savar Upazila"), level = "thana",
         district = c("Gazipur", NA, "Feni", NA), warn = FALSE)
bd_place(c("Ashulia", "Mirpur"), level = "thana", district = "Dhaka",
         details = TRUE)
```

Every name that was not written in the standard spelling is listed in the
message, so corrections (especially fuzzy typing-error corrections) can be
checked. Names used in several districts need the district; without it they
are "ambiguous" and `NA`, not guessed.

## Addresses

```{r}
bd_address(c("House 12, Road 5, Mirpur 10, Dhaka-1216",
             "Vill: Char Kalia, P.O: Kalia, Narail - 7520",
             "Ashulia, Dhaka", "Kaliganj", "Mirpur, Dhaka-7030"))
```

## Whole data frames

```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  mobile  = c("01712345678", "+880 1812-345678", "12345", "N/A"),
  zila    = c("Chittagong", "Jessore", "Dhaka", "Atlantis"),
  income  = c("Tk 25,000", "1.5 lakh", "15-20k", "-"),
  address = c("Agrabad, Chattogram 4100", "Kotwali, Jessore", "Ashulia", NA),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
spec <- c(mobile = "phone", zila = "district", income = "amount",
          address = "address")
bd_check(df, spec, district = "zila")
bd_check(df, spec, details = TRUE, district = "zila")
bd_clean(df, spec, district = "zila")
```

`bd_check()` tells you what cannot be read and why; `bd_clean()` adds the
cleaned columns next to the originals, so nothing is overwritten unless you
ask for it with `suffix = ""`.
